sourceFacts.floorCount: Map and catalog describe 43 levels; ABT describes 44. The engineer explicitly identifies the unserved technical floor 27A. These conventions remain distinct.
sourceFacts.reviewScope: Static medium-fi exterior preserves the unchanged original493066-triangle detailed draft and supplies a separate reviewed terracotta-soffit source correction with four complete browser levels. Published152.317m tip and8m weather vane are retained, with a fixed documented M pose. Three structural zones, offset brick/pale volumes, circular windows, recessed glazed loggias, connecting terraces, braced open quay cantilever, roof tank sculpture and parked crane are retained. Exact43/44floor conventions,27A technical floor, individual floor heights, pale-panel substrate, balcony depths, entrance details and roof equipment proportions remain reconstructed. 2022BAG roof envelope has2.20mRMSE. GroundNAP3.279 is estimated, not surveyed. Hidden interiors, underground parking, adjoining buildings, vessels and surrounding quay are excluded; real host pavement/quay fitting is required and footprint replacement is disabled.

reconstruction.envelope: Regularized BAG plan with separate shifted upper volume; noisy roof polygons are reference evidence rather than imported mesh.
reconstruction.facade: Bay widths, staggered windows, individual floor elevations, service equipment and sculpture proportions are reconstructed from linked photographs and drawings. Pale panel substrate is unconfirmed; the shared concrete graph approximates its matte finish.
reconstruction.vane: A fixed documented pose for reproducibility; the real M rotates with the wind.
reconstruction.soffit: Terracotta-colored rectangular underside panels observed in architect20190429-153624 photograph; canonical concrete graph supplies shared panel finish with source-local red tint, composition unconfirmed.

nativeAxes.origin: BAG plan envelope center; Y0 is terrain contact. Native+X east-northeast follows the AntoinePlatekade edge and native+Z south-southeast faces the Rijnhaven. Actual north-up Google satellite viewed2026-10-09 shows tall tower at the southwest negative-X end, lower projecting wing at the northeast positive-X end, terraces between and quay on the southeast. Architect river overview and cantilever photograph independently show that signed arrangement. The glass-fronted low-wing cantilever remains open below over the pedestrian quay; the BAG perimeter is an upper-volume projection, not a ground solid. RD-to-WGS84 operation accuracy1m and approximately3degree heading uncertainty describe reconstructed placement, not a surveyed azimuth.

appearance.identity: Rotterdam’s Montevideo: offset brick and pale tower volumes, an upper fifteen-level glazed balcony frame, lower circular windows, a stepped connecting block, the braced quay cantilever, rooftop water-tank sculpture and open lattice M weather vane.
appearance.master: Historical draft preserved; terracotta soffit tint repaired in source-local reviewed recipe.
appearance.browser: Complete massing, open quay cantilever, offset upper volume, loggias, circle-window marks, roof tank and open M weather vane at every level.
